questions.question: There are three taps of diameters 3 cm, 5 cm, and 6 cm respectively. The rate of water flow through them is proportional to the square of their diameters. The largest tap alone can fill a tank in 72 minutes. If all three taps are opened together, in how many minutes will they fill the tank?
questions.questionHtml: There are three taps of diameters 3 cm, 5 cm, and 6 cm respectively. The rate of water flow through them is proportional to the square of their diameters. The largest tap alone can fill a tank in 72 minutes. If all three taps are opened together, in how many minutes will they fill the tank?
questions.solution:
Let diameters be:

D₁ = 3 cm, D₂ = 5 cm, D₃ = 6 cm

Flow rate ∝ diameter²

So relative flow rates:

Tap 1: 3² = 9 units

Tap 2: 5² = 25 units

Tap 3: 6² = 36 units

Total flow rate when all taps open = 9 + 25 + 36 = 70 units Tap 3 alone fills tank in 72 min → 36 units in 72 min

So, tank capacity = 36 × 72 = 2592 units

Time to fill with all taps = 2592 ÷ 70 = 37(2/70) = 37(1/35) minutes

Final Answer: 37(1/35) minutes

questions.question: A container has 80 L of a mixture of milk and water in the ratio 7:3. If 20 L of this mixture is replaced with pure milk, what will be the new ratio of milk to water?
questions.questionHtml: A container has 80 L of a mixture of milk and water in the ratio 7:3. If 20 L of this mixture is replaced with pure milk, what will be the new ratio of milk to water?
questions.solution:
Initial quantities

Total mixture = 80 L

Milk = (7/10) × 80 = 56 L

Water = (3/10) × 80 = 24 L

Remove 20 L of mixture in same ratio

Milk removed = (7/10) × 20 = 14 L

Water removed = (3/10) × 20 = 6 L

Remaining after removal:

Milk = 56 – 14 = 42 L

Water = 24 – 6 = 18 L

Add 20 L of pure milk

New milk quantity = 42 + 20 = 62 L

Water remains = 18 L

New ratio of milk to water

= 62 : 18

Divide both by 2 → 31 : 9

Final Answer: 31 : 9

questions.question: Sejal wishes to use a stick of length 15 units as common internal tangent to two circles of radius three units and five units. What can be the maximum distance (in units) between the centres of the circle?
questions.questionHtml: Sejal wishes to use a stick of length 15 units as common internal tangent to two circles of radius three units and five units. What can be the maximum distance (in units) between the centres of the circle?
questions.solution:
Let distance between centres = d

For internal tangent:

Length = √[d² − (r₁ + r₂)²]

⇒ 15 = √[d² − (3 + 5)²]

⇒ 15 = √(d² − 64)

Square both sides: 225 = d² − 64

⇒ d² = 289

⇒ d = √289 = 17

Final Answer: 17 units

questions.question: A circle is inscribed in a rhombus with diagonals 15 cm and 20 cm. Find the diameter of the circle.
questions.questionHtml: A circle is inscribed in a rhombus with diagonals 15 cm and 20 cm. Find the diameter of the circle.
questions.solution:
Given rhombus with diagonals 15 cm and 20 cm.

Area = (d₁ × d₂) / 2
= (15 × 20) / 2 = 150

Side = √[(d₁/2)² + (d₂/2)²]
= √[(7.5)² + (10)²]
= √(56.25 + 100)
= √156.25 = 12.5

Semiperimeter = (4 × side) / 2 = (50) / 2 = 25

Inradius r = Area / s = 150 / 25 = 6

Diameter = 2r = 12 cm

questions.question: Two cars are approaching each other from a distance of 18 km. Each car travels at 60 km/h. A bird sitting on the roof of the first car starts flying toward the second car at 90 km/h. The bird reaches the second car, immediately turns and flies back to the first car, and continues shuttling back and forth until the two cars collide. What total distance (in km) does the bird travel?
questions.questionHtml: Two cars are approaching each other from a distance of 18 km. Each car travels at 60 km/h. A bird sitting on the roof of the first car starts flying toward the second car at 90 km/h. The bird reaches the second car, immediately turns and flies back to the first car, and continues shuttling back and forth until the two cars collide. What total distance (in km) does the bird travel?
questions.solution:
Time until cars collide

Relative speed = 60 + 60 = 120 km/h

Time to collide = Distance ÷ Relative speed = 18 ÷ 120 = 0.15 hours

Distance flown by bird

Bird flies for 0.15 hours at 90 km/h

Distance = Speed × Time = 90 × 0.15 = 13.5 km

Final Answer: 13.5 km

questions.question: (x−2) boys can do a piece of work in ‘x’ days and (x+7) boys can do 75% of the same work in (x−8) days. Then in how many days (x+10) boys finish the work?
questions.questionHtml: (x−2) boys can do a piece of work in ‘x’ days and (x+7) boys can do 75% of the same work in (x−8) days. Then in how many days (x+10) boys finish the work?
questions.solution:
Let total work = W units.

From first case:

(x − 2) × x = W ⇒ W = x(x − 2)

From second case: (x + 7)(x − 8) = 75% of W

⇒ (x + 7)(x − 8) = (3/4)x(x − 2)

Solve:

(x + 7)(x − 8) = (3/4)(x² − 2x)

⇒ x² − x − 56 = (3/4)(x² − 2x)

⇒ 4x² − 4x − 224 = 3x² − 6x

⇒ x² + 2x − 224 = 0 ⇒ x = 14 (valid root)

Now, total work = 14 × 12 = 168 units

(x + 10) = 24 boys ⇒ 24 units/day

Time = 168 / 24 = 7 days

Answer: 7 days

questions.question: Cost price of 15 articles is equal to the selling price of 10 articles. The discount given on 12 articles is equal to the profit earned on 6 articles. Find the difference between the profit % and the discount %.
questions.questionHtml: Cost price of 15 articles is equal to the selling price of 10 articles. The discount given on 12 articles is equal to the profit earned on 6 articles. Find the difference between the profit % and the discount %.
questions.solution:
Let cost price per article = C

15C = 10×SP ⇒ SP = 1.5C

Profit per article = SP−C = 0.5C ⇒ profit% = (0.5C/C)×100 = 50%

Let marked price = M

Total discount on 12 articles = 12×(M−SP)

Profit on 6 articles = 6×(SP−C) = 3C

So 12(M−1.5C) = 3C ⇒ M−1.5C = 0.25C ⇒ M = 1.75C

Discount% = [(M−SP)/M]×100 = (0.25C/1.75C)×100 = 100/7 = 14(2/7)%

Difference = 50% − 14(2/7)% = 35(5/7)%

Answer: 35(5/7)%

questions.question: A square pyramid has a base of 12 cm and a slant height of 10 cm. Find the total surface area?
questions.questionHtml: A square pyramid has a base of 12 cm and a slant height of 10 cm. Find the total surface area?
questions.solution:
Area of base (square)

= side × side

= 12 × 12

= 144 cm²

Area of one triangular face

= (1/2) × base × slant height

= (1/2) × 12 × 10

= 60 cm²

Area of four triangular faces

= 4 × 60

= 240 cm²

Total surface area

= Area of base + Area of four triangles

= 144 + 240

= 384 cm²

Final Answer: 384 cm²

questions.question: A cylindrical vessel of internal radius 7 cm and height 24 cm is completely filled with water. This water is then poured into a cuboidal tank of internal dimensions 21 cm × 14 cm × h cm such that the tank is exactly filled. Find the approximate value of h.
questions.questionHtml: A cylindrical vessel of internal radius 7 cm and height 24 cm is completely filled with water. This water is then poured into a cuboidal tank of internal dimensions 21 cm × 14 cm × h cm such that the tank is exactly filled. Find the approximate value of h.
questions.solution:
Volume of cylindrical vessel

= π × r² × h

= (22/7) × 7² × 24

= (22/7) × 49 × 24

= 22 × 7 × 24

= 3696 cm³

Volume of cuboidal tank

= length × breadth × height

= 21 × 14 × h

= 294h cm³

Equating volumes

294h = 3696

⇒ h = 3696 / 294

⇒ h ≈ 12.57 cm

Final Answer: Approximately 12.57 cm

questions.question: A shopkeeper marks his goods 60% above cost. He then offers successive discounts of 20% and 25% on the marked price. He also uses a faulty scale that shows 1 kg when it is actually 900 g, and finally gives a 5% cashback on the amount paid. What is his overall approximate profit percentage?
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper marks his goods 60% above cost. He then offers successive discounts of 20% and 25% on the marked price. He also uses a faulty scale that shows 1 kg when it is actually 900 g, and finally gives a 5% cashback on the amount paid. What is his overall approximate profit percentage?
questions.solution:
Let cost price (CP) of 1 kg of goods = ₹100

Step 1: Marked Price (MP)

= CP + 60% of CP

= ₹100 + ₹60 = ₹160

Step 2: Apply successive discounts: 20% and 25%

First discount: 20% of ₹160 = ₹32 → New price = ₹160 − ₹32 = ₹128

Second discount: 25% of ₹128 = ₹32 → Final selling price before cashback = ₹128 − ₹32 = ₹96

Step 3: Apply 5% cashback

Cashback = 5% of ₹96 = ₹4.80

Net amount paid by customer = ₹96 − ₹4.80 = ₹91.20

Step 4: Faulty scale effect

Customer thinks he got 1 kg, but actually received only 900 g

So effective cost to shopkeeper = 900 g = 0.9 kg × ₹100 = ₹90

Step 5: Profit = Net received − Cost

= ₹91.20 − ₹90 = ₹1.20

Step 6: Profit percentage

= (Profit / Cost) × 100

= (1.20 / 90) × 100 = 1.33%

Final Answer: Approximately 1.33% profit

questions.question: Find the equation of the line passing through (2, –3) and perpendicular to the line 3x – 4y + 7 = 0.
questions.questionHtml: Find the equation of the line passing through (2, –3) and perpendicular to the line 3x – 4y + 7 = 0.
questions.solution:
Find slope of the given line

Given: 3x – 4y + 7 = 0

⇒ Rewrite in slope form: y = (3/4)x + 7/4

⇒ Slope (m₁) = 3/4

Slope of perpendicular line

⇒ m₂ = –1 / m₁ = –4/3

Use point-slope form with point (2, –3)

⇒ y + 3 = –(4/3)(x – 2)

⇒ y + 3 = –(4/3)x + (8/3)

⇒ y = –(4/3)x + (8/3) – 3

⇒ y = –(4/3)x – (1/3)

⇒ 3y = –4x – 1

⇒ 4x + 3y + 1 = 0

Correct Option: 4x + 3y + 1 = 0

questions.question: In a game show, there are 3 doors: behind one is a car, behind the other two are goats. You pick one door. The host, who knows what’s behind the doors, always opens one of the other two doors to reveal a goat, then offers you the chance to switch to the remaining unopened door. What are your chances of winning the car if you (i) stay, (ii) switch?
questions.questionHtml: In a game show, there are 3 doors: behind one is a car, behind the other two are goats. You pick one door. The host, who knows what’s behind the doors, always opens one of the other two doors to reveal a goat, then offers you the chance to switch to the remaining unopened door. What are your chances of winning the car if you (i) stay, (ii) switch?
questions.solution:
Initial pick: P(car) = 1/3, P(goat) = 2/3.
Host always opens a goat door and never opens the car door.
• If your initial pick was car (prob 1/3), switching loses.
• If your initial pick was goat (prob 2/3), host is forced to reveal the other goat, so switching wins.
Therefore: Stay wins with probability 1/3; Switch wins with probability 2/3.

Answer: A) Stay: 1/3, Switch: 2/3

questions.questionHtml: Ramesh's average earning per month in the first four months of a year was ₹12,500. In May, his earning was 20% more than the average earning in the first four months. Earnings in first 4 months
Average = 12,500

May’s earning
= 12,500 × 1.20 = ₹15,000

Total Jan–May
= 50,000 + 15,000 = ₹65,000

Whole year total (12 months)
= 14,200 × 12 = ₹170,400

June–Dec (7 months)


= 170,400 – 65,000 = ₹105,400

Average for June–Dec
= 105,400 ÷ 7 = ₹15,057.14

questions.question: The following are the marks of 8 students: 18, 20, 22, 25, 27, 30, 35, 40 Find the Semi-Interquartile Range (Quartile Deviation).
questions.questionHtml:
The following are the marks of 8 students:
18, 20, 22, 25, 27, 30, 35, 40

Find the Semi-Interquartile Range (Quartile Deviation).
questions.solution:
Given data (sorted): 18, 20, 22, 25, 27, 30, 35, 40

Number of observations (n) = 8

Find Q1 (First Quartile)

Position of Q1 = (n + 1) / 4 = (8 + 1) / 4 = 2.25

Q1 lies between 2nd and 3rd values:

Q1 = 20 + 0.25 × (22 - 20) = 20 + 0.5 = 20.5

Find Q3 (Third Quartile)

Position of Q3 = 3(n + 1) / 4 = 3(8 + 1) / 4 = 6.75

Q3 lies between 6th and 7th values:

Q3 = 30 + 0.75 × (35 - 30) = 30 + 3.75 = 33.75

Semi-Interquartile Range (Quartile Deviation)

= (Q3 - Q1) / 2

= (33.75 - 20.5) / 2

= 13.25 / 2

= 6.625

Final Answer: 6.625
